POLITICAL AND INSTITUTIONAL OVERVIEW


MACROECONOMIC OVERVIEW

Tailwinds
Plan México
Creates a national framework for investment attraction, regional development, and industrial upgrading (> $277 Bn USD envisioned across 2,000+ projects). 

North American integration
Mexico remains a top U.S and Canadian trade partner.

Alignment to 2026 USMCA review 
Strengthening North American integration positioning and trilateral cooperation. 

Exports in traditional sectors
Prioritized under Plan México: EVs, semiconductors, aerospace, medical devices, clean energy, logistics, digital economy. 

Regulatory efficiency agenda
Including a goal to sharply trim approval times and strengthen legal clarity for priority sectors. 

Sectoral and regional diversification
With major new investment flows in chemicals, energy infrastructure, logistics, and advanced manufacturing clusters across the North, Bajío and Southeast. 
Headwinds
Security costs
Acting as an “insecurity tax” (20% of firm sales absorbed by crime prevention + damages). 

Investment performance 
Since mid 2024 due to trade uncertainty, legal concerns, energy bottlenecks and high operating costs. 

Policy environment
Around trade and tariffs (especially U.S. actions), undermining investment planning.

Nearshoring opportunity
Of China’s 8-pp loss in U.S imports, Mexico captures only 2pp. 
Most gains went to Southeast Asia, especially Vietnam and Taiwan.  

Energy policy
After reversal of the 2013 energy reform, discouraging private investment and slowing sector modernization.
